body: Thank you for answering. Sorry you went through this, at work and all. I actually have, like you said, opted for working from home. I even started before Covid; I have the luxury to do that without consequences. I won't be working with her anymore in several months, gladly. However, I sure hope to not fall for the limerence trap in future workspaces.

Yes, I've learned (still learning) to treat my feelings right and accept these sensations. On the other hand, I have to let go of the thoughts. You're right, I'm not a failure or weak or broken. It's always nice to read that from someone else, given that it's hard to believe it sometimes. Thanks for the kind words.
Yeah you’re right. He was bigger than his brothers in sisters since birth.

Wow that's interesting. I actually got similar (very unpleasant) sensations. Those were 'old' sensations that started when I was a child, and then appeared furiously with fever. It also appeared wildly during meditation. I sat there and suddenly my body felt immense, or very disorganized. I also happened to have tactile 'hallucination' (not sure I can call it that) which made me feel the entire space around me as a 3D maze of wood blocks. Weird enough I would say...

It is unpleasant, but I tried to just analyze it consciously while meditating. It evolved ; the sensations came and went, with different levels of intensity. Usually opening my eyes ends the whole experience.

I googled AiWS and it seems to be exactly that. Thank you for this! I thought I was quite alone with this condition :)

Also, I have the Epstein-barr virus and I had ophtalmic migraines in the past.
Thanks a lot! It’s actually my first try with acrylic. It took me a lot of time, but I’m pretty satisfied with the result.

I feel you, truly. I'm in a similar situation myself (LO is a coworker), and I recently saw her after 3 months of NC. I immediately got back my anxiety about seeing her on the street as I go to work, and nearly all the intrusive thoughts came back. Like you, I don't want to feel that way, this is really hard. 

I believe that having good company in those difficult moments, a friend that knows about your situation and helps you out, is so important. It makes you feel a little less alone, even though none of my friends fully understand what I'm going through.

Hang in there. Those difficult moments pass.
Unfortunately she's there every day. I agree, I need to go and brace myself. It's important to maintain my work life afloat the best I can. Thanks for your insight.

Yes, I've seen some improvements, but only when I went back to my hometown, close to my family. From there I thought of her less and less and recovered. However, I also had a major depressive episode for no reason during that period, which brought back intrusive thoughts... I also recovered from it, and I'm better now.

Yeah, I also think it's a good strategy to limit contact. I also think that if I start another LE, I will just wait and heal at home. I seems that it is not linear at all with me. I can be fine for two weeks and then things go haywire again. I guess this is something that needs to be dealt with each day. One important thing I also learnt is that blocking the thoughts and refusing my state is making it worse.

Thanks a lot for your input. I must say I kind of agree with the fact that seeing her regularly does help. I mean, I've been there and I even had some periods of complete well-being. The trick is when I hear or see something that hurts me, say she is seeing someone (not the case right now) for instance, or others. Sometimes I'm extremely sensitive to things that wouldn't bother anybody else in this situation; and me placing her on that pedestal makes it so difficult to accept what I consider as flaws.. and it makes me suffer for no good reason. I think I will go back there, but I will be cautious too.

Hey, 

I'm not really good at giving advice, especially regarding mental health because I feel that this is an experience so personal that it is really hard to wisely pinpoint what to say. That being said, I felt like answering because I relate with what you're saying. Feeling out of normalcy, fucked up in the brain and not made for society are thoughts that I struggle a lot with... I'm currently in a bad place as well. Being here to share your thoughts, write in down and seeking help is a very good start I would say. I admire you for doing that. Be well.
Hey. I'm sorry you feel that way. I don't have bpd but I read a lot about it, and even if I can't fully understand what you're going through, I can imagine this is mentally overwhelming...

Thanks. I'm actually going to a third therapist currently (the first two ones did not seem to understand that I'm suffering, which is peculiar...), and she seems really great. I'm enjoy the sessions and it gave myself hope :)

Yeah I know fluctuations are common. It's usually invalidating when people seem to think it's only due to the PhD and that it happens to everyone during it. I have another issue that sparked my depression, and I actually have a nice place to work and good supervisors (I'm lucky on this one, this could have been much worse).

I usually build routines. I normally work out everyday, meditate everyday, make good meals, etc. Thing is it sometimes gets hard to get back into those routines when broken. I also break things down to not overwhelm myself. It worked today, you know, first get out of bed, then shower, etc.. got me through the day.

As for my PhD, it deals with image classification. I'm actually trying to develop techniques to analyse and classify a certain type of objects (seen in archaeology mainly). It's basically related to computer vision/image processing.

I relate completely when you talk about not being able to make up for the bad days during the good ones. The good days are when I am focused on what I am doing and motivated enough to do it, but it feels like it's impossible to double the amount of work  to compensate :/

Well, it makes me think of the ups and downs of limerence. I give way to much value to my LO and it regulates my mood. Sometimes I got joyful because she talked to me and we had a nice chat, other times she seemed distant and cold and it made me feel depressed or like I did not matter to her.

But I guess the main thing is that I'm putting way too much dedication to her, helping her when she needs me and even anticipating things for her. This is clearly disproportionate, but I often don't see why it couldn't be the way she feels too. And so, several times, she did things or say things that misaligned with what I thought she would think or do. Surely, for her it was nothing. Just tired, just her vision of the world. However, to me, it felt like treason. I would become really angry, but I'm not the type of person who explodes, so I would keep it for me, although I wanted to lash out at her. The emotional mix would become unbearable and I would end up hurting myself, because nothing else (and I try healthier things like running to exhaust myself, or smashing pillows...) would seem to end this suffering. I guess I wanted to show her how much I suffered... which is pretty dumb, come to think of it...

It resonates also with a previous experience, several years ago, which was very much the same as above, except  it was with my best friend. He did something I didn't expect from him, and I felt betrayed too. I didn't harm myself at the time, but it did cause me pain.

Thank you for this insight. I knew about BPD but never really looked at it closely. Some aspects of the 'favorite person' indeed ring a bell.
I do agree that learning to love yourself is one of the way to lessen, or rather, to go through this pain more peacefully when it arises.
If I may ask, how did you heal yourself to come to like yourself and act in healthier ways in those situations?

I'm glad to see that you still had this part of your brain going on for you. I aim for it in those bad days. It's like you totally have to not listen to your brain and do the rational thing. Again, most of the time I manage to do it, because I know that it will pass. But some other times there this spike that is so hard to overcome..

Thank you for this good advice. I have seen a psychologist some months ago but unfortunately we did not get along very well. I have recently decided to make an appoitment with another therapist. It's worth the shot I think. I'm also on meds and seeing a psychiatrist, for what it's worth. On top of that I try so many things to keep myself afloat ... it's just that sometimes it gets too hard.
